content: 1. For the treatment of active duodenal ulcers in adults, the recommended oral dosage of Famotidine is 40 mg once daily at bedtime. Most patients achieve healing within 4 weeks, and it is rarely necessary to continue full dosage for more than 6 to 8 weeks. 2. For maintenance therapy of duodenal ulcers in adults, the recommended oral dosage is 20 mg once daily at bedtime. 3. For the treatment of active benign gastric ulcers in adults, the recommended oral dosage of Famotidine is 40 mg once daily at bedtime for up to 6 weeks. In some cases, therapy may be extended to 12 weeks if necessary. 4. In pediatric patients aged 3 months to less than 1 year with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), the recommended dosage is 5 mg/kg per dose administered twice daily. The use of intravenous Famotidine in pediatric patients under 1 year of age with GERD has not been adequately studied. 5. Published uncontrolled studies suggest Famotidine may be effective in treating GERD and peptic ulcers in pediatric patients. However, data are insufficient to establish precise response rates based on dose and duration of therapy. Treatment duration and dosage should be individualized based on clinical response, pH monitoring (gastric or esophageal), and endoscopy findings. 6. In pediatric patients, doses up to 1 mg/kg/day for peptic ulcers and 2 mg/kg/day for GERD (with or without esophagitis, including erosions and ulcerations) have been used in published studies. 7. For pathological hypersecretory conditions, such as Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome, the recommended starting oral dose for adults is 20 mg every 6 hours. In some cases, higher starting doses may be required. Dosages should be adjusted to meet individual patient needs and continued as long as clinically indicated. Doses up to 160 mg every 6 hours have been administered to some adult patients with severe Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome. 8. Famotidine oral suspension can be substituted for Famotidine tablets for any of the approved indications. 9. Famotidine orally disintegrating tablets can also be substituted for Famotidine tablets at the same recommended dosages for any of the approved indications. 10. Antacids may be administered concomitantly with Famotidine if needed. 11. In adult patients with moderate renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <50 mL/min) or severe renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <10 mL/min), the elimination half-life of Famotidine is prolonged. In severe cases, it may exceed 20 hours, reaching approximately 24 hours in anuric patients. 12. To avoid excessive accumulation of the drug in patients with moderate or severe renal insufficiency, the dosage of Famotidine may be reduced to half the usual dose, or the dosing interval may be extended to 36 to 48 hours, depending on the patient’s clinical response. 13. Based on pharmacokinetic comparisons between adults and pediatric patients, dosage adjustments should also be considered for pediatric patients with moderate or severe renal insufficiency.
